zh.summary: 從真實工作經過找需求：比較問卷、訪談與觀察，以五步流程釐清問題，分清功能、易用性與工作成效的證據。
objectives: 將工具經驗調查與工作需求問題分開。
改寫誘導式問題，詢問具體工作事件。
從合成回答建立訪談追問、假設與需求紀錄，不宣稱已取得真實使用者證據。

readingGuide.goal: 用現況調查找到值得追問的問題，保留回答、推論與驗證的區別。
readingGuide.startingPoint: 先閱讀一段明確標為虛構的缺件經驗，不需要採訪真實業務。
readingGuide.route: 先用看診類比理解訪談，再比較三種調查方式、練習五步流程，最後用案例、三層驗證與樣本偏差判讀需求。
readingGuide.output: problem.md 的需求線索附錄：調查問題、訪談追問、假設與驗證動作。

sections.heading: 學員調查也是需求訪談：白話文完整教學
paragraphs: 這一課最重要的觀念是：
不要一開始就問別人「你想要什麼功能」，而是先了解「你現在怎麼工作、哪裡遇到困難，以及為什麼困難」。
因為使用者告訴你的，不一定是真正的需求；有時候，他只是描述一個症狀，甚至直接提出一個未必有效的解法。
舉例來說，有人說「我希望有 AI 幫我檢查文件」，我們不能直接認定他需要 AI。真正的問題可能只是：系統沒有設定必填欄位。

sections.heading: 一、先理解：為什麼要做需求訪談？
paragraphs: 想像你是一位醫生。
病人走進診間，告訴你：「醫生，我需要吃抗生素。」
你會直接開抗生素嗎？
當然不應該。因為抗生素是病人認為的「解決方法」，卻不是診斷結果。
你應該先問他：「哪裡不舒服？從什麼時候開始？有沒有發燒？之前發生過嗎？」
軟體工程其實非常相似。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜醫師看診與需求訪談
blocks.description: 共同原則：先診斷問題，再決定解法。 兩欄是平行類比；醫療欄只用來說明先了解問題的思路。

items.title: 醫師看診
items.body: 病人：「我要吃抗生素。」 醫師先了解症狀、病史與檢查結果，再決定治療方式。

items.title: 需求訪談
items.body: 使用者：「我要一套 AI 系統。」 工程師先了解工作流程與困難，再決定是否需要 AI。

blocks.heading: 訪談要確認的工作情境
paragraphs: 所以，需求訪談（Requirements Interview）的目標，不是蒐集一張「大家希望增加哪些功能」的購物清單。
真正的目標是了解：誰在什麼情況下，想完成什麼工作，遇到了什麼阻礙？

sections.heading: 二、問卷、訪談、觀察，有什麼不同？
paragraphs: 假設你要替一個有 100 位員工的單位改善文件收件系統。
你可以使用三種方式蒐集資訊：

blocks.caption: 表 1｜問卷、訪談與觀察的用途
rows: 問卷 Survey
向多人提出相同問題
哪些問題值得優先研究？
訪談 Interview
找人深入聊真實經驗
問題為什麼發生？
觀察 Observation
看人實際執行工作
人實際上怎麼做？

blocks.heading: 100 位員工的文件收件案例
paragraphs: 例如問卷顯示有 40 位受訪者說「處理文件很慢」。這只代表這些受訪者有這樣的感受。
你找其中幾位訪談後，才知道有人在等系統載入，有人在重複輸入資料，還有人在等主管簽核。
接著，你實際觀察操作流程，發現員工經常在三個畫面之間來回切換、複製相同資料。
這時候，你才逐漸掌握真正的問題。
簡單來說：問卷讓你知道可能有什麼問題；訪談讓你理解原因；觀察幫助你核對實際行為。

sections.heading: 三、為什麼「怎麼問」，會影響答案？
paragraphs: 下面是兩種問法。
不好的問法
「如果我們開發 AI 自動檢查系統，是不是就可以大幅改善你們的效率？」
這叫引導式提問（Leading Question）。它預設 AI 有效，還暗示受訪者應該回答「是」。
比較好的問法
「你上一次發現文件資料有缺漏時，從發現到完成補件，實際發生了什麼事情？」
這是開放式、以經驗為基礎的問題。受訪者可以描述真正的工作狀況，而不需要先同意某種技術解法。
受訪者可能回答：「上次交接時，發現承辦人漏填文件種類。我打電話找他，結果他正在開會，隔天才補好。」
現在你就得到更有價值的線索：問題不只在於漏填欄位，也包含補件通知、等待時間，以及交接流程。

sections.heading: 四、需求訪談最重要的五個步驟
paragraphs: 先保留原話，再追問事件、確認需求、提出假設，最後安排驗證。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜需求訪談的五個步驟
blocks.description: 箭頭表示調查與驗證的工作順序，不代表每一步已經得到證實。第③步的需求仍須向使用者確認，第⑤步比較操作時間和錯誤次數。

items.title: ① 聽到原話
items.body: 「我們的系統很慢。」

items.title: ② 追問真實經過
items.body: 「最近一次慢，是在哪個步驟？」

items.title: ③ 定義真正的需求
items.body: 「希望減少重複填寫相同資料。」

items.title: ④ 提出改善假設
items.body: 「讓資料自動帶入，可能減少工作量。」

items.title: ⑤ 實際驗證
items.body: 「試用原型，比較操作時間和錯誤次數。」

blocks.heading: 先確認「慢」發生在哪裡
paragraphs: 這五個步驟最容易犯錯的地方，是直接從第一步跳到第四步。
例如有人說「系統很慢」，工程師馬上決定升級 GPU、換資料庫，甚至改用更快的 AI 模型。
但「系統很慢」至少有四種不同情況：

blocks.caption: 表 2｜四種「慢」與可能改善方向
rows: 按鈕按下去要等 20 秒
檢查伺服器、網路、資料庫及程式效能
相同資料要輸入三次
自動帶入資料、減少重複步驟
不知道下一步該按哪裡
改善 UI／UX、資訊架構及操作引導
必須等主管批准兩天
改善簽核流程、通知與代理機制

blocks.heading: 依原因選擇改善方向
paragraphs: 你會發現：四種問題都叫「慢」，但解決方式完全不同。
這也是為什麼軟體工程不能只懂程式，還需要理解人如何工作。

sections.heading: 五、完整案例：替單位設計文件缺漏檢查工具
paragraphs: 我們來看一份假想訪談記錄。
使用者說：「每次到交接時，我才發現有人沒填文件類型，常常又要打電話去問。」
工程師應該把資料分開記錄：

blocks.heading: 原始事實｜受訪者說了什麼
paragraphs: 「交接時才發現文件類型沒填，要再問一次送件者。」

blocks.heading: 待確認的解釋｜工程師怎麼理解
paragraphs: 可能是送件階段缺少檢查，也可能是交接前沒有複核。

blocks.heading: 改善假設｜不代表已經有效
paragraphs: 在交接前提醒缺漏欄位，可能減少來回補件。

blocks.heading: 驗證計畫｜怎麼知道有沒有改善
paragraphs: 先確認必填規則，再製作簡單原型，觀察使用者能否找到缺漏、理解提示、完成修正，並比較前後流程。

blocks.heading: 固定規則先用表單驗證
paragraphs: 注意，這個例子不一定需要 AI。
如果文件類型就是固定的必填欄位，只需要設定表單驗證規則，就可能解決問題。
例如：
這是介面提示的片段；documentType 與 showError 由既有應用提供。正式系統也須在伺服器端核對必要欄位，避免略過介面檢查。

blocks.heading: 什麼情況需要進一步研究 AI？
paragraphs: 這段簡單的程式可能就足夠了。沒有必要為了看起來先進，硬加入大型語言模型（LLM）。
但如果必填規則會因文件內容、案件類型或特殊情境而改變，就可能需要進一步研究規則引擎、文件解析，甚至 AI 輔助判斷。
需求決定技術，不是技術決定需求。

sections.heading: 六、做出功能，還不代表解決需求
paragraphs: 這裡要區分兩種測試：
功能測試（Functional Testing）是確認程式有沒有按照規格執行。例如文件類型未填時，畫面確實出現錯誤提示。
易用性測試（Usability Testing）則是確認真正的使用者能不能理解並完成工作。例如提示出現後，他是否知道要去哪裡修改，以及能不能自行完成交接。
兩者都通過後，還可以進一步做成效驗證（Outcome Evaluation）：實際補件次數是否減少？平均處理時間是否縮短？是否反而產生新的錯誤？
因此有三個不同層次：

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜三種證據分別回答不同問題
blocks.description: 三層各需自己的測試與觀察；功能通過，不能直接推論人能使用或工作已改善。圖中上下位置用來比較證據，不表示成效已發生。

items.title: 系統正確
items.body: 功能是否按規則運作？

items.title: 人能使用
items.body: 使用者是否能理解、操作並完成任務？

items.title: 工作改善
items.body: 錯誤、等待或工作成本是否實際下降？

blocks.heading: Coding Agent 的完成回報能證明什麼？
paragraphs: 尤其在 AI 協作開發裡，Coding Agent 告訴你「功能已完成」，通常只能表示它認為已經完成某些開發任務，不能證明使用者的問題被解決。

sections.heading: 七、調查結果要怎麼解讀，才不會過度推論？
paragraphs: 假設你辦了一場課程，100 位學員裡面只有 3 位填寫問卷，而且這 3 位都說希望學 AI Coding。
你能得到什麼結論？
可以說：「三位回覆者都對 AI Coding 有興趣，值得進一步了解。」
不能說：「100 位學員都希望學 AI Coding，因此我們已經證明這是最受歡迎的課程。」
因為另外 97 位沒有回答，而且這 3 位可能剛好都是已經有程式背景的人。
這涉及樣本偏差（Sampling Bias）。調查結果可能受到誰願意回答、誰有機會回答、回覆者屬於哪一類人的影響。
同樣地，問卷沒有填名字，也不能自動視為匿名。若內容包含特殊職務、案件日期或具體工作事件，仍可能辨識當事人。
所以正式訪談要留意資料用途、告知與同意、紀錄權限、保存期限，以及個人資訊最小化。課堂練習則可以直接使用合成案例。

sections.heading: 八、把 M01-03 與 M01-04 接起來
paragraphs: 上一課 M01-03 告訴我們：
從個人工具變成多人共用系統，必須思考權限、資料、協作、錯誤處理，以及誰負責維護。
這一課 M01-04 接著告訴我們：
這些事情不能全靠工程師想像，必須向實際使用的人確認。
例如設計一個文件收件系統時，送件者、承辦人、複核人、主管及系統管理員可能都有不同需求。
如果只訪談主管，可能做出管理者喜歡、但第一線人員很難操作的系統。
因此，需求訪談也是一種跨角色的工作流程調查。
這一課真正要培養的能力，就是能夠把「使用者提出的功能願望」轉化為「可以被確認、實作與驗證的工作需求」。這也是從單純寫程式，走向真正的軟體工程與產品設計的重要一步。

blocks.heading: 下一步：整理需求線索
paragraphs: 把調查線索接到 M03 的 problem.md，分別寫出回答來源、你的解釋、待確認問題與下一個驗證動作。

exercise.environment: 文字編輯器與本課提供的合成回答；不需建立問卷網站或收集真人資料。
steps: 在 problem.md 的需求線索小節寫三個問題，分別了解工具操作、工作事件及目前優先困難，逐題註明用途。
將一題含「你是不是也覺得」的誘導問法，改成開放、中立、可追問最近事件的問題。
使用本課合成回答，分欄記錄回答內容、你的解釋、待確認假設與下一步驗證。
請同儕試讀提問，指出是否預設答案、是否可能要求個資，再修正問題。
exercise.expected: 一份有用途說明的調查題目，以及合成回答到訪談追問、假設與驗證的對照。
exercise.check: 同儕能分清哪些是合成回答、哪些是你的推論，以及哪一項需要後續觀察；沒有把示範結果稱為真實訪談發現。
exercise.cleanup: 只保留合成回答與去識別化回饋；若誤填真實姓名、業務細節或聯絡資料，移除後再分享。

en.summary: Find requirements in actual work: compare surveys, interviews and observation, investigate problems in five steps, and distinguish functional, usability and outcome evidence.
objectives: Separate questions about tool experience from questions about work needs.
Rewrite leading questions to ask about concrete work events.
Use synthetic answers to develop follow-up questions, assumptions and requirements records without claiming actual user evidence.

readingGuide.goal: Use a current-state survey to identify questions worth pursuing while separating answers, interpretations and verification.
readingGuide.startingPoint: Read a missing-document experience clearly labeled as fictional; no actual business interview is needed.
readingGuide.route: Start with the medical analogy, compare three research methods, practice the five-step process, then examine the worked case, three evidence layers and sampling bias.
readingGuide.output: A requirements-leads appendix in problem.md containing survey questions, interview follow-ups, assumptions and verification actions.

sections.heading: A Learner Survey Is Also a Requirements Interview
paragraphs: The central idea of this lesson is:
Before asking people which features they want, understand how they work now, where they struggle and why.
What users tell you may describe a symptom or propose a solution that will not work; it does not necessarily identify the underlying requirement.
For example, someone might say, “I want AI to check documents.” This does not establish a need for AI. The actual problem might simply be that the system has no required-field validation.

sections.heading: 1. Why Conduct Requirements Interviews?
paragraphs: Imagine you are a doctor.
A patient walks into your office and says, “Doctor, I need antibiotics.”
Would you prescribe them immediately?
You should first investigate. Antibiotics are the patient’s proposed solution, not a diagnosis.
Ask: “What symptoms do you have? When did they start? Have you had a fever? Has this happened before?”
Software engineering follows a similar approach.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Medical Consultation and Requirements Interview
blocks.description: Shared principle: diagnose the problem before choosing a solution. The columns are parallel analogies; the medical example illustrates the order of investigation only.

items.title: Medical consultation
items.body: Patient: “I want antibiotics.” The doctor reviews symptoms, history and examination results before choosing treatment.

items.title: Requirements interview
items.body: User: “I want an AI system.” The engineer investigates the workflow and difficulties before deciding whether AI is needed.

blocks.heading: The Work Situation to Confirm
paragraphs: A requirements interview aims to understand work, rather than merely collect a shopping list of requested features.
Ask: who is trying to accomplish which task, in what situation, and what gets in the way?

sections.heading: 2. How Do Surveys, Interviews and Observation Differ?
paragraphs: Suppose you are improving document intake for an organization with 100 employees.
You can gather information in three ways:

blocks.caption: Table 1 | Surveys, Interviews and Observation
rows: Survey
Ask many people the same questions
Which issues deserve investigation first?
Interview
Discuss actual experiences in depth
Why does the problem occur?
Observation
Watch people carry out their work
What do people actually do?

blocks.heading: Document Intake for 100 Employees
paragraphs: For example, 40 survey respondents say that document handling is slow. This establishes how those respondents feel about the work.
Interviews with some of them reveal different situations: waiting for screens to load, re-entering data or waiting for a supervisor’s approval.
You then observe the workflow and find employees repeatedly switching among three screens and copying the same data.
These steps gradually clarify the actual problem.
A survey identifies possible issues; interviews investigate why they arise; observation checks what people actually do.

sections.heading: 3. Why Does the Way You Ask Affect the Answer?
paragraphs: Compare these two ways of asking.
A leading question
“If we built an AI system to check documents automatically, wouldn’t it greatly improve your efficiency?”
This is a leading question: it assumes AI will work and suggests that the respondent should agree.
A better question
“The last time you discovered missing document information, what actually happened from discovery to completion of the missing information?”
This is an open question grounded in experience. Respondents can describe their work without first endorsing a technical solution.
A respondent might say: “At the last handoff, I found that the case handler had left out the document category. I called, but they were in a meeting, so it was completed the next day.”
This gives you useful leads about notifications, waiting and handoff, as well as the missing field.

sections.heading: 4. Five Steps in a Requirements Interview
paragraphs: Retain the original words, investigate the event, confirm the need, propose a hypothesis and arrange verification.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | Five Steps in a Requirements Interview
blocks.description: Arrows show the investigation and verification sequence, not established findings. Confirm the need in step 3 with users; compare task time and error counts in step 5.

items.title: ① Record the original words
items.body: “Our system is slow.”

items.title: ② Ask about the actual event
items.body: “At which step was it slow the last time?”

items.title: ③ Define the underlying need
items.body: “We want to avoid entering the same information repeatedly.”

items.title: ④ Propose an improvement hypothesis
items.body: “Automatically filling existing data may reduce the work.”

items.title: ⑤ Verify in practice
items.body: “Try a prototype and compare task time and error counts.”

blocks.heading: Locate the Meaning of “Slow”
paragraphs: A common mistake is jumping directly from step one to step four.
For example, an engineer hears “the system is slow” and immediately decides to upgrade the GPU, replace the database or use a faster AI model.
Yet “slow” can describe at least four different situations:

blocks.caption: Table 2 | Four Meanings of “Slow” and Possible Improvements
rows: Wait 20 seconds after pressing a button
Check server, network, database and code performance
Enter the same data three times
Fill existing data automatically and reduce duplicate steps
Do not know what to press next
Improve UI/UX, information architecture and guidance
Wait two days for supervisor approval
Improve approval flow, notifications and delegation

blocks.heading: Choose an Improvement for the Cause
paragraphs: All four problems are described as “slow,” but call for different improvements.
This is why software engineering requires understanding how people work as well as knowing how to program.

sections.heading: 5. Worked Example: A Tool for Checking Missing Document Information
paragraphs: Consider this fictional interview record.
The user says: “At handoff, I keep discovering that someone left the document type blank, and I often have to call to ask.”
The engineer should record these layers separately:

blocks.heading: Reported account | What the respondent said
paragraphs: “At handoff, I discovered that the document type was blank and had to ask the sender again.”

blocks.heading: Unconfirmed interpretation | How the engineer understands it
paragraphs: There may be no intake check, or no review before handoff.

blocks.heading: Improvement hypothesis | Effectiveness is not yet established
paragraphs: A reminder about missing fields before handoff may reduce repeated requests for missing information.

blocks.heading: Verification plan | How to check whether work improves
paragraphs: Confirm which fields are required, build a simple prototype, observe whether users can find omissions, understand prompts and correct them, and compare the workflows before and after.

blocks.heading: Use Form Validation for a Fixed Rule
paragraphs: This example may not require AI.
If document type is always required under a fixed rule, form validation may solve the problem.
For example:

This is a UI prompt fragment; the existing application supplies documentType and showError. A production system must also validate required fields on the server so that interface checks cannot be bypassed.

blocks.heading: When Should You Investigate AI Further?
paragraphs: This small piece of code may be sufficient. Adding a large language model (LLM) just to appear advanced is unnecessary.
If required-field rules vary with document content, case type or special circumstances, investigate a rules engine, document parsing or AI-assisted judgment further.
Choose technology according to the requirement.

sections.heading: 6. A Working Feature Does Not Yet Establish a Solved Need
paragraphs: Distinguish two kinds of testing:
Functional testing checks whether code follows its specification. For example, leaving document type blank must display an error prompt.

Usability testing checks whether actual users can understand the interface and complete their work. After seeing the prompt, do they know where to correct the field, and can they complete handoff independently?
Once both pass, evaluate outcomes: do actual requests for missing information decrease? Does average processing time fall? Have new errors appeared?
These are three different layers:

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Three Kinds of Evidence Answer Different Questions
blocks.description: Each layer needs its own tests and observations. A functional pass does not establish usability or improved outcomes. Vertical positions compare evidence; they do not claim an improvement has occurred.

items.title: System correctness
items.body: Does the feature follow its rules?

items.title: Usability
items.body: Can users understand, operate and complete the task?

items.title: Work outcomes
items.body: Have errors, waiting or work costs actually decreased?

blocks.heading: What Does a Coding Agent’s Completion Report Establish?
paragraphs: In AI-assisted development, a Coding Agent saying “the feature is complete” usually means it considers certain development tasks finished. That does not establish that the user’s problem has been solved.

sections.heading: 7. How Can You Interpret Survey Results Without Overgeneralizing?
paragraphs: Suppose only 3 of 100 course participants answer a survey, and all 3 want to learn AI Coding.
What can you conclude?
You can say: “All three respondents are interested in AI Coding; this deserves further investigation.”
You cannot say: “All 100 participants want AI Coding, so we have proved it is the most popular course.”
The other 97 people did not answer, and the 3 respondents might all happen to have programming experience.
This involves sampling bias. Who is willing to answer, who has an opportunity to answer and which groups respondents belong to can affect the findings.
Likewise, omitting names does not automatically make a survey anonymous. A distinctive role, case date or specific work event may still identify someone.
For real interviews, consider data purpose, notice and consent, recording permissions, retention periods and personal-data minimization. Classroom exercises can use synthetic cases.

sections.heading: 8. Connect M01-03 and M01-04
paragraphs: M01-03 explained:
Moving from a personal tool to a shared system requires attention to permissions, data, collaboration, error handling and maintenance ownership.
M01-04 adds:
Engineers need to confirm these matters with the people doing the work.
For example, senders, case handlers, reviewers, supervisors and system administrators may have different requirements for document intake.
Interviewing only supervisors may produce a system that managers like but frontline staff struggle to use.
A requirements interview therefore also investigates workflows across roles.

This lesson develops the ability to turn feature wishes into work requirements that can be confirmed, implemented and verified. That ability supports software engineering and product design beyond writing code.

blocks.heading: Next: Record Requirements Leads
paragraphs: Connect the leads to M03’s problem.md and record the answer source, your interpretation, unanswered questions and the next verification action.

exercise.environment: A text editor and the supplied synthetic answer. No survey website or actual participant data is needed.
steps: In the requirements-leads section of problem.md, write three questions about tool operation, a work event and the current highest-priority difficulty, explaining each question’s purpose.
Rewrite one leading question containing “don’t you also think” as an open, neutral question about a recent event.
Using the synthetic answer, separately record the answer, your interpretation, an unconfirmed hypothesis and the next verification action.
Have a peer read the questions for assumed answers or possible requests for personal data, then revise them.
exercise.expected: Purposeful survey questions and a mapping from a synthetic answer to interview follow-ups, hypotheses and verification.
exercise.check: A peer can distinguish the synthetic answer from your interpretations and identify what needs later observation. Demonstration results are not labeled as actual interview findings.
exercise.cleanup: Retain only synthetic answers and de-identified feedback. Remove any accidentally entered names, business details or contact information before sharing.

zh.prompt: 某位同事說：「我希望我們單位引進 ChatGPT，這樣一定能提升效率。」你應該先問什麼？
options: 最近一次工作遇到困難，具體發生什麼事？
rationales: 先了解工作問題，再判斷是否需要模型及哪一種模型。
先追問最近的實際經過，才能找到需求線索。
GPU 預算屬於解法與資源，還不能解釋工作困難。

en.prompt: A colleague says, “I want our organization to adopt ChatGPT; it will definitely improve efficiency.” What should you ask first?
options: What exactly happened the last time you encountered a difficulty at work?
How many GPUs can the budget buy?
rationales: Understand the work problem before choosing whether a model is needed or which one to use.
A recent actual event provides requirements leads.
GPU budget concerns a solution and resources, not the cause of the work difficulty.

zh.prompt: 一位使用者說「系統很慢」，你應該如何處理？
options: 追問最近一次操作經過，找出真正的瓶頸
rationales: 伺服器效能只是可能原因之一，需先找到瓶頸。
介面可能影響操作，但應先確認實際卡點。
追問事件能區分等待、重複輸入、操作引導與簽核問題。

en.prompt: A user says, “The system is slow.” What should you do?
options: Immediately switch to a faster server
Ask about the most recent task and identify the actual bottleneck
rationales: Server performance is only one possible cause; locate the bottleneck first.
The interface may affect the task, but first confirm where work gets stuck.
An event account distinguishes waiting, duplicate input, guidance and approval problems.

zh.prompt: 三位自願回覆者都提到補件問題，你可以推論什麼？
options: 補件是所有人最大的問題
補件值得繼續調查，但還不能代表所有使用者
AI 已被證明可以解決補件問題
rationales: 三位自願回覆者不足以代表所有人。
可以繼續調查補件問題，並確認其他角色與未回覆者的經驗。
調查只提供問題線索，尚未測試 AI 解法。

en.prompt: Three voluntary respondents all mention requests for missing information. What can you infer?
options: Missing information is everyone’s biggest problem
Missing information deserves further investigation, but these respondents do not yet represent all users
AI has been proved to solve missing-information requests
rationales: Three voluntary respondents do not represent everyone.
Investigate missing-information requests further and include other roles and nonrespondents.
The survey offers problem leads; it has not tested an AI solution.
